newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to seek harbour deregulation, cargo fee cut.
newsitem.headline: Japan to seek harbour deregulation, cargo fee cut.

text.p: The Japanese government said on Tuesday it will seek the deregulation of harbour services and a cut in cargo-handling charges as part of its bid to give foreigners better access to Japanese markets.
Economic Planning Agency officials said that the port deregulation will be included in a package of 19 measures to be adopted by the government to improve market access.
The decision to review current rules was made at a meeting of the government's Office of Trade and Investment Ombudsman, they said.
Japan will also simplify import regulations for medical equipment, cosmetics and medicine, as well as review quarantine inspections and customs services at ports, they said.

The United States has charged that Japan has unfair port practices which discriminate against foreign firms, and has said it will retaliate by slapping a surcharge from April 14 on each Japanese vessel entering a U.S. port from abroad.
